ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, several students are doing a “rope-shaking power generation” experiment on the school playground: the two ends of a relatively long electric wire are connected to two terminals on a sensitive galvanometer, forming a closed circuit. Two students stand respectively along the east-west direction, the girl stands on the west side, and the boy stands on the east side; they rapidly shake this electric wire up and down along the vertical direction. Suppose that at the position shown in the figure, the direction of the geomagnetic field is parallel to the ground, pointing from south to north. Which of the following statements is correct
ready1_open_rewrite.title: Multi-Physics open-ended question 1
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the “rope-shaking power generation” experiment, suppose the direction of the geomagnetic field is parallel to the ground and points from south to north. When the electric wire moves downward, which point has a higher electric potential among points A and B in the figure?
ready1_open_rewrite.expected_answer: The electric potential at point B is higher than the electric potential at point A

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the “rope-shaking power generation” experiment, suppose the direction of the geomagnetic field is parallel to the ground and points from south to north. When the electric wire moves downward, which point has a higher electric potential among points A and B in the figure?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: The electric potential at point B is higher than the electric potential at point A
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure, a long electric wire is being shaken at both ends by two students; the left endpoint is marked A, and beside it is the girl; the right endpoint is marked B, and beside it is the boy. The two ends of the electric wire form a closed circuit with a sensitive galvanometer through the wire below. Then reason: the problem statement says the girl is on the west side and the boy is on the east side, so A in the figure is the west end of the electric wire, and B is the east end of the electric wire. Take east as +x, north as +y, and vertically upward as +z. The geomagnetic field is horizontal and points from south to north, that is, the magnetic field direction is +y; when the electric wire moves downward, the velocity direction is −z. Judge the force direction on a positive charge using the Lorentz force q(v×B): v×B = (−z)×(+y) = +x, that is, pointing east. Therefore positive charges are pushed toward the east end B, the B end accumulates positive charge, and its electric potential is higher than that of the west end A.
